records.supported_name_scope: Rio Caí is representative of the principal middle and lower river and its connected upper Santa Cruz corridor. records.geographic_disambiguation: This is not the upper Rio dos Sinos or its Paranhana main route. In the terminal region, Caí, Sinos, Jacuí, Gravataí and Guaíba are separately depicted; the stored terminal class sea is retained model metadata and does not establish an open-ocean mouth.

records.supported_name_scope: Rio Real is repeatedly printed on the long middle/lower border river and its estuarine continuation; primary mapping connects the separately identified Heliópolis headward drainage to this river. The support is for the representative system.
records.region: Bahia–Sergipe border, Brazil; Heliópolis feeder/Jibóia–Cumbanzê–Real corridor to the inner Real estuary.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The entire selected FID corresponds, at ordinary generalized scale, to a Heliópolis headward feeder–Jibóia/Cumbanzê–Rio Real corridor. The long downstream river follows the Bahia–Sergipe border through the Tobias Barreto/Itapicuru setting, then southeast past Rio Real municipality and east past Jandaíra to the lower estuarine widening near Indiaroba. Original INEMA and CPRM maps, supplemented by the original IBGE Heliópolis and Jandaíra municipal sheets, cover the complete selected corridor, major tributary settings and actual modeled terminal setting. Rio Real is supported as the representative system identity; it is not imposed on the initial feeder, upper differently labeled reaches or the whole outer estuary.

naming_scope_details.actual_selected_terminal: Widening inner Rio Real estuary near Indiaroba, upstream of the Pontal/Mangue Seco Atlantic entrance
component_scope_limits: The headward portion belongs to the rural Heliópolis feeder network and Riacho da Jibóia/Cumbanzê drainage. It is not renamed Rio Real merely because the downstream river has that name.

The initial minor headward reach has no securely established hydronym in the inspected source coverage; its name remains null. Map correspondence was assessed at ordinary generalized corridor scale, without a precise source-point or name-transition-vertex claim.

INEMA's regional sheet generalizes the upper junctions; IBGE's 2010 municipal sheet distinguishes Riacho da Jibóia and the receiving Cumbanzê corridor before the Rio Real border reach. These labels are retained as bounded component observations rather than reconciled into a single scalar name.

The selected downstream end lies within the widening Rio Real estuarine corridor near Indiaroba, upstream of Pontal/Mangue Seco and the open-Atlantic entrance. The retained model terminal class sea does not establish that the selected line reaches the ocean-mouth point.
The Piauí/Fundo branches and their shared outer estuary are receiving-setting context, not extra selected reaches or alternate whole-feature names.
All accepted, scalar, Korean and application fields remain null or false. No formal registry status is claimed.

reconstruction_rule: Start from the pinned r46 cumulative index and apply later append-only deltas in verified commit order, rejecting duplicate IDs. Keep base records, scope clauses, region qualifiers and assessment histories unchanged. Apply explicit status-list changes. Subtract all recorded IDs from the exact eligible initial inventory to recover unrecorded targets; pending IDs remain recorded but are not completed source reviews.
publication_boundary: Own factual name/scope findings, public official URLs, bounded geometry metadata and public continuity pins only. No original maps, crops, complete coordinates or private source/derivative/registration fingerprints. Official hosting does not establish source redistribution rights.

research_order.progress_rule: Follow the actual continental order: Americas, Asia, Africa, Europe, then other, with all rivers before lakes. Preserve original queue IDs and ranks for continuity; apply documented geographic deferrals without counting them as name research, and place deferred objects into their corrected later phase by length-descending, stable-ID order. Prior candidate and scope-held assessments remain unresolved where stated.
